correctness.rationale: Independent Gaussian maxima at each positive mesh point divided by √(2 log N) converge to √t by the two-sided normal tail asymptotics. The Brownian reflection bound plus the union bound over N paths and a fixed mesh gives maximum normalized increments ≤ε with probability tending to one when mesh width δ<ε². This also handles t=0 and proves uniform convergence in probability on compacts. The exact minimum process is ℓ+√(2Dρ_N)B₀−2√(Dq_N)Y_N. If q_N→a<∞ then ρ_N→1 and the limit starts positive and hits in finite time, no later than the ordinary Brownian hit. Strong Markov and local Brownian downward oscillations at the first hit dominate the local O(h) barrier increment, ensuring continuity of the first-crossing map. In the divergent regime, rescaling time by ℓ²/(4Dq_N) gives a common noise coefficient at most (2q_N)⁻¹ᐟ² and the uniform deterministic limit 1−√u, whose crossing is strict. For survival of T_a set b=√(2a), c=ℓ/√(2D); logarithmic time makes the boundary b−ce^(−s/2) for the stationary OU process. The killed generator is unitarily equivalent to the Dirichlet confining Schrödinger operator −∂²/2+x²/8−1/4. This gives discrete spectrum and a positive ground state. Moving the wall gives continuous eigenvalues via translation and the variational principle, and strict domain monotonicity follows because a zero extension cannot be the positive ground state on the larger domain. The upper survival bound uses the fixed wall b−ε from a sufficiently late time. The lower bound starts at a finite time in a compact interval above b, with positive prior survival probability (use a Brownian tube around a steep linear path starting at zero and staying strictly above b√r−c); the initial surviving submeasure is dominated by the stationary Gaussian and has positive ground-state overlap. Killing at b then gives a bound C t^(−λ(b)), which is essential at the critical exponent. Lower and upper bounds yield the claimed logarithmic exponent. On (1,∞), x²−1 is a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction with eigenvalue 1, so monotonicity gives finite mean precisely at b>1, including divergence at equality.
residual_risks: The threshold concerns only the limiting random variable. No uniform integrability or finite-N mean result follows. The verification script's Gaussian quadrature and OU finite differences are numerical; fixed-time positivity is not first-passage survival.

Treat the square-root-boundary tail problem and eigenvalue/mean argument as classical background applied to that limit, not as a standalone novelty claim. The independent-search scale and several different shared environments are already known; no inspected statement or demonstrated implication covers the specified growing-N crossover.

value.rationale: The result tells when many Brownian searches average away their independent fluctuations yet retain order-one environmental randomness in the fastest time. It identifies the scale at which the usual accelerating independent limit gives way to a nondegenerate random law, and the sharp moment consequence makes that law qualitatively interpretable. This is more informative than pointwise Gaussian extremes or a fixed-number correlation calculation.
residual_risks: Restricted to additive global Brownian noise with equicorrelation, common initial distance and zero drift; no extrapolation to general dependent populations.
